concept.name: Long put butterfly
concept.definition: A long put butterfly is a three-strike, same-expiration spread built from puts only: long one put at a higher strike, short two puts at a middle strike, and long one put at a lower strike, with the middle strike equidistant from the wings. Entered for a small net debit, its expiration payoff matches the long call butterfly at the same strikes, peaking when the underlying finishes at the middle strike.
concept.intuition: The same target bet as the call butterfly, assembled from puts instead — by put-call parity the two structures are economically equivalent at identical strikes.
concept.mechanics: Net debit = (higher put + lower put) - 2 x middle put; the position is worth zero outside the wings and peaks at the wing width at the body strike. It decomposes into a bear put spread plus a bull put spread sharing the short middle strike.
concept.formula: Value at expiration = max(0, min(K3 - S_T, S_T - K1)) when K2 - K1 = K3 - K2; max value = K3 - K2 at S_T = K2; max loss = net debit.
concept.failure_modes: Identical structural weaknesses to the call butterfly: a narrow profit zone, heavy relative transaction costs, and short-gamma whipsaw risk around the body strike near expiration; put-side skew can make the put version priced differently in practice.
concept.misconceptions: The call and put butterflies are not different bets — put-call parity makes their expiration payoffs identical at the same strikes, so the choice between them is about pricing and liquidity, not payoff shape.
concept.example: Buy the $105 put, sell two $100 puts, buy the $95 put for a $1.00 net debit. Max value $5.00 at $100; outside $95-$105 the debit is lost; breakevens at $96 and $104.
